Rather single monolithic Dragen tool bundling every schema, tidydragen gives group tool (DragenMap, DragenCov, DragenVar, DragenRna, DragenFqc, DragenTso), reasons: Pipelines produce different subsets. germline-run somatic SV RNA fusion outputs; RNA-run variant calling. Dragen workflow registers six tolerates absent files, pipeline simply yields tables , --nothing coupling. One tool, one schema.yaml, one output category. tool owns single, focused schema scoped group; tool name becomes category token every output name (e.g. <prefix>_dragencov_finehist), table’s origin self-documenting. Independent evolution. Adding, versioning, fixing one group’s schema touches tool, keeping shared metrics logic DragenTool base untouched. shared machinery still lives one place. Everything common (dragen-metrics/csv-nohead filetypes, refine_files prefix logic, fail-loud policies) sits DragenTool base inherited , splitting tools costs duplication.
